analysis.investment_thesis: CSSL operates in India's growing integrated facility management market with 24% revenue CAGR, but net profits are actually declining and free cash flow is deeply negative — the story doesn't hold up under the hood. Lynch's cardinal rule: earnings must back up the growth narrative.
key_strengths: Revenue momentum is real: 309 → 476 Cr (+54% in 2 years), with operating income doubling from 15 → 31 Cr
ROCE of 20.4% suggests the core business earns decent returns on capital employed
High promoter holding (73%) aligns management with long-term outcomes
key_risks: Net profit actually FELL in FY25 (12 → 10 Cr) despite 37% revenue growth — margin compression driven by finance costs tripling (4 → 10 Cr)
Free cash flow collapsed to -26 Cr in FY25; OCF positive only 1 of 3 years — this is a serial cash burner
Debt nearly tripled in one year (53 → 128 Cr), pushing D/E to ~0.94, well above Lynch's 0.6 comfort level
red_flags: PEG ratio is effectively undefined/infinite — earnings are declining, not growing, making P/E of 18.8x on falling profits look expensive
Other income flipped from +3 Cr to -2 Cr in FY25, suggesting write-offs or losses on investments masking weak core performance
Total assets doubled (153 → 327 Cr) while equity grew only 57% — leverage-funded expansion in a wafer-thin margin business (~2% net) is high-risk
analysis.detailed_analysis:
CSSL looks like a fast grower on the revenue line, but Peter Lynch's first question is always: "Show me the earnings." Here, net profit went backward — from 12 Cr to 10 Cr — as the company took on massive debt (128 Cr borrowings) and saw finance costs surge. Operating margins are thin at ~6.5%, and net margins compressed to 2.1% in FY25. The P/E of 18.8x on declining earnings is not the GARP bargain it superficially appears; the PEG ratio is meaningless when earnings growth is negative.

The cash flow story is the real dealbreaker. FCF of -26 Cr on a 243 Cr market cap means the company is consuming 10%+ of its market cap annually in cash just to sustain operations — classic "profits on paper, burning cash in reality" profile common in low-margin services with working capital intensity. CWIP jumped to 22 Cr suggesting capital commitments ahead. I'd want to see two consecutive years of positive OCF and a credible path to debt reduction before considering this. Facility management is a legitimate secular growth story in India, but CSSL's balance sheet discipline needs to improve materially first.
